correctness.rationale: For alpha,beta,gamma,mu>0 and compactly supported flow-invariant probability nu, the generator identities Lz=mu*x, Ly=gamma*y*(x^2-1), L(z^2)=2*mu*x*z and L(x^2)=2*alpha*x^2*(1-y)-2*beta*x*z establish E[x|z]=0, y(E[x^2|y]-1)=0, E[xz]=0 and E[x^2]=E[x^2*y]=E[y]. Since y(t) never changes sign, a hypothetical invariant mass in y<0 yields an invariant normalized restriction with E[y]<0 but E[y]=E[x^2]>=0, contradiction. On y=0 the (x,z) matrix [[alpha,-beta],[mu,0]] has strictly positive-real-part eigenvalues, hence its only bounded full orbit is (0,0); the only stationary plane mass is the origin atom w. Conditional integration gives E[x^2]=E[y]=1-w. On y>0 an invariant measure with |x|<=1 or |x|>=1 a.s. must have x^2=1 a.s.; no complete compact invariant orbit can then have constant x=+/-1 and z prime=mu*x nonzero. Periodic orbit mean x=0 from z prime gives at least two x=0 crossings, and mean x^2=1 plus nonconstancy gives at least two |x|=1 crossings. All statements are necessary for compact invariant states; no existence of nontrivial attractors asserted.
residual_risks: The conclusion is conditional on compactly supported invariant measures, not existence of non-equilibrium compact recurrence for every parameter set.
